description: Structural schema for one mission manifest. Optional keys not listed here are allowed (top-level additionalProperties is true). Semantic rules stay in manage_backlog.py: priority-score arithmetic and projected_impact path safety. DEVIATIONS FROM THE KEYWORD SET: 'exclusiveMinimum' is used for cost_weight (must be > 0), and 'propertyNames' is used for related_missions keys (must match ^MISSION-\d{3}$). Neither can be expressed with the listed keywords alone.

id.description: Mission identifier in the form MISSION-NNN.

execution_surface.description: Where the mission runs: a local machine, a hybrid setup, a cloud worker, or multiple repositories.

target_platform.description: The platform, system, or artifact the mission measures or changes.

created_at.description: Creation time in UTC, formatted YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.

updated_at.description: Last update time. Accepts the Z form and the offset form with optional fractional seconds (for example 2026-11-05T04:44:35.171601+00:00), because existing manifests written by the closure tooling use the offset form.

confidence_reviewed.description: Date the confidence scores were last reviewed, formatted YYYY-MM-DD.

falsification_criteria.description: Observable outcomes that would refute the hypothesis.

baseline_evidence.description: Prior measurements or facts the hypothesis builds on.

experiment.description: Path or reference to the experiment directory or plan.

scores.description: Scoring dimensions used to rank the mission.

strategic_leverage.description: Integer 1 to 5: how much the mission moves the project forward.

epistemic_depth.description: Integer 1 to 5: how much new knowledge the mission is expected to produce.

operational_friction.description: Integer 1 to 5: expected operational difficulty or friction.

cost_weight.description: Number greater than 0 and at most 1: relative cost weight of the mission.

priority_score.description: Priority score computed from the dimensions above, as stored by the backlog tooling.
Top-level priority score as stored by the backlog tooling. Its arithmetic is checked in manage_backlog.py, not here.

model_routing.description: Which model tier and model should run the mission.

cheapest_viable_tier.description: Cheapest model tier expected to succeed on this mission.

recommended_model.description: Model identifier recommended for the mission.

cli_target.description: CLI or runtime that executes the recommended model.

cost_weight.description: Relative cost weight for routing decisions.

fallback_models.description: Ordered list of fallback model identifiers.

frontier_escalation_condition.description: Condition under which the mission should escalate to a frontier model, or a note that escalation does not apply.

verdict.description: Outcome of the hypothesis test; null while unresolved. CONFIRMED is a LEGACY value used by 6 resolved missions and is accepted for those records.

human_gate_required.description: Whether a human must approve the mission before it proceeds.

issue_ref.description: Linked issue reference, or null when none exists.

assignee.description: Agent or person currently assigned to the mission.

worktree.description: Git worktree in which the mission is being executed.

lessons_learned.description: Short lessons recorded when the mission closes.

evidence.description: Evidence records supporting the verdict. Each item is a citation string or an object with fields such as timestamp, agent, citation and details.

reference_doctrines.description: Doctrine or protocol documents referenced by the mission.

phases.description: Ordered phases of the mission plan.

related_missions.description: Map from related MISSION-NNN identifiers to the relationship description. Keys must match ^MISSION-\d{3}$.

projected_impact.description: Declared footprint of the mission on the repository. Structure only; path-safety rules are enforced in manage_backlog.py.

paths.description: Non-empty list of repository paths, directories or globs the mission will touch.

resources.description: Shared resource identifiers the mission will use.

shared_generated.description: Generated shared files the mission will rewrite.
